title: No deal between AstraZeneca and BMS, senior source insists: Reuters
snippet: Reuters has deflated rumors that AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb are discussing a possible merger, letting the air out of industry-wide speculation over what could have been the largest deal in pharma history.

title: Bespoke gene-editing outfit abandons lead program, cuts ‘several’ employees
snippet: Seven months after launching with $16 million in seed financing, Jennifer Doudna’s Aurora Therapeutics is pivoting away from its lead indication, phenylketonuria, owing to growing competition in the field.

title: Over 1/3 stay in biopharma jobs for health insurance, poll finds
snippet: A recruiter and career coach discuss when and why some biotech and pharma professionals put a premium on health insurance benefits.

title: Pfizer ramps up ongoing restructuring, Lisata axes 72% of staff
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Gilead looks to upcoming inflammation, cancer catalysts as pressure to diversify mounts
snippet: HIV remained Gilead’s strongest franchise in the second quarter, but the pharma is building out its pipeline beyond virology, particularly focusing on inflammation and oncology.

title: Lilly’s $23B Q2 soars over expectations but Foundayo lags Novo’s rival oral GLP-1
snippet: Eli Lilly’s shares rose nearly 5% to $1,170 apiece in premarket trading as the company reported $23 billion in revenue for the second quarter. The company’s market cap is $1.02 trillion as of the end of July.

title: 2026 IPO stock tracker: How newly public biotechs are performing
snippet: BioSpace is launching an IPO dashboard to help the industry keep tabs on U.S. biotechs that have taken the public plunge in 2026.

title: Amgen’s MariTide stands alone after obesity cull while analysts seek more M&A
snippet: Amgen has discontinued Phase 1 obesity candidate AMG 513, leaving MariTide as its sole weight loss asset. Meanwhile, executives said the company’s late-stage pipeline is largely full and future business development will focus on earlier-stage opportunities.

title: Novo CEO sees innovation as a matter of survival amid pipeline setbacks
snippet: Novo Nordisk CEO Maziar Mike Doustdar on a second quarter earnings call argued that failure is par for the course in the drug development business. The Danish pharma is focused on building out its pipeline to move past recent clinical roadblocks.

title: Rumors of biggest pharma merger ever drop amid Q2 earnings, contentious FDA adcomms
snippet: The industry has been abuzz since the weekend when talks of a potential mega-merger between Bristol Myers Squibb and AstraZeneca were reported. Meanwhile, Pfizer, Merck and others release second quarter earnings, with some disclosing pipeline discontinuations and cost-cutting measures. Finally, all eyes turn to the FD...

title: 5 NextGen winners who went public this year (and which ones are hiring)
snippet: BioSpace NextGen honorees made up one-third of the U.S. biotechs that have publicly debuted in 2026. Most are looking for biopharma professionals to join their teams.

title: 4 potential biotech M&A targets, plus a pretty sure bet from J&J
snippet: Pharma is definitely interested in making more deals. But what biotechs will come under the magnifying glass? BioSpace takes a look at companies that analysts see as near-term targets for buyouts.

title: Novo dips 6% on Wegovy pill stumble despite Q2 earnings beat
snippet: Novo Nordisk’s shares fell 6% on Tuesday afternoon after its second quarter earnings report showed a slight miss for the Wegovy pill vs. consensus.

title: Lisata axes 72% of workforce following failed merger with Kuva
snippet: In addition to laying off employees, including a member of its management team, Lisata Therapeutics is also suing Kuva Labs, alleging the company breached a merger agreement.

title: Pfizer CEO defends $7B bolt-on M&A strategy as peers rush to buy
snippet: Asked on a second quarter earnings call if Pfizer could direct more money to M&A amid a feeding frenzy across the pharma industry, CEO Albert Bourla defended his strategy.

title: Merck’s $10.8B Prometheus deal delivers another win—plus a Phase 2b miss
snippet: The anti-TL1A antibody from Merck's 2023 Prometheus buy delivered positive mid-stage results in a skin condition but failed in a certain type of lung disease, the Big Pharma revealed alongside second-quarter earnings.

title: BioNTech cuts sales forecast on slumping demand for COVID-19 vaccine
snippet: Lower vaccine demand across every market and more acute pressures in Germany led BioNTech to lower the midpoint of its sales outlook by almost 20%.

title: As portfolio erodes, BMS stands to gain a lot from rumored AstraZeneca merger
snippet: While both drugmakers face looming patent cliffs, analysts say joining forces could help Bristol Myers Squibb replenish its eroding portfolio—while the strategic case for AstraZeneca seems to be more mixed.

title: Pfizer cuts $2.5B more across R&D, manufacturing in ongoing restructure
snippet: The additional cuts, which will primarily occur between 2027 and 2029, will cost some $6 billion as the pharma tries to ride out a post-COVID headache while facing stiff patent headwinds for major products like the blood thinner Eliquis.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
